Four relaxed-to-balanced days in Kyoto that start with an easy Gion evening on arrival. They cover Fushimi Inari, the eastern temples, Arashiyama and the Golden and Silver Pavilions, then finish with a short morning at Nijo Castle and Nishiki Market before you leave. Stops are grouped by district to keep transit short, and the total comes to roughly ¥153,000, well inside the ¥400,000 budget.

Five days in Tokyo that pair classic sights (Senso-ji, Tokyo Tower, Skytree, Meiji Jingu) with a teamLab and Ghibli day and a slower Shinjuku and Aoyama day. The plan assumes you land on the evening of the 3rd, so day one is a light night-view loop. You stay in central Ginza, and the total comes in well under the ¥600,000 budget.

A three-day Osaka trip that arrives in the afternoon for Shinsekai and the neon of Dotonbori, spends the middle day on the castle, the aquarium and a sunset view over Umeda, and ends with a gentle shrine-and-market morning before departure. Every meal is at a vegan kitchen to keep the trip vegetarian, and the total stays well inside the 250,000 JPY budget.

A two-day Tokyo trip with the Ghibli Museum, Senso-ji and a few classic Tokyo sights. Day 1 is an afternoon-and-evening loop from Asakusa to Shibuya, and Day 2 is a relaxed morning at the Ghibli Museum followed by lunch and a shrine walk. The total comes to roughly ¥118,000 against the ¥200,000 budget.

Day 1 (2027-09-18): Senso-ji, Tokyo Skytree, Afuri Ebisu, Shibuya Crossing.

A compact two-day Osaka trip built around Osaka Castle on arrival day, followed by the neon of Dotonbori after dark. Day 2 is a lighter morning of a shrine and the retro Shinsekai district, leaving room for the journey home. Every meal is at a fully vegetarian kitchen, and the plan stays well under budget.
